package_info.why_malicious: The affected Struts2 versions contain a critical deserialization vulnerability in the REST plugin's XML handling. Attackers can submit specially crafted XML payloads that exploit insecure deserialization via the XStream library, resulting in remote code execution (RCE) on the server. This allows attackers to execute arbitrary system commands and gain full control over vulnerable systems.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, during HTTP request processing to REST endpoints
execution_context.file_location: Struts2 REST plugin (XML deserialization via XStream library)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the server receives an HTTP request containing a crafted XML payload, the XStream library deserializes the XML into a java.lang.ProcessBuilder object, which results in the execution of attacker-supplied system commands on the server, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted XML input directly into Java objects allows attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes, such as java.lang.ProcessBuilder, and execute system commands. This behavior is highly suspicious because it enables attackers to run arbitrary code on the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects XML input to be parsed as data and mapped to safe, expected object types, not to instantiate classes with side effects or execute system commands. Deserializing user-supplied XML into unrestricted Java objects violates secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve deserializing XML from trusted, authenticated sources with strict type whitelisting, ensuring only safe object types are allowed. Accepting and deserializing arbitrary XML from untrusted users is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Deserialization of user-supplied XML via XStream without type restrictions
Presence of java.lang.ProcessBuilder or other sensitive classes in XML payload
Execution of system commands as a result of XML deserialization
Lack of input validation or type whitelisting in REST endpoint configuration

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted XML payload containing a serialized java.lang.ProcessBuilder object to a Struts2 REST endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: The server receives the malicious XML and passes it to the XStream library for deserialization.

attack_chain.action: XStream deserializes the XML payload, instantiating the attacker-controlled java.lang.ProcessBuilder object.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deserialization triggers the execution of arbitrary system commands on the server.

attack_chain.action: The system command specified by the attacker is executed on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution and full control over the vulnerable server.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted XML input via XStream in Struts2 REST endpoints
Unexpected instantiation of java.lang.ProcessBuilder or other sensitive classes from XML payloads
Execution of system commands triggered by HTTP POST/PUT requests to REST endpoints
Application logs showing errors or stack traces related to XStream deserialization
file_indicators: struts.xml or struts-rest.xml configuration files enabling the REST plugin
References to com.thoughtworks.xstream.XStream in application source code
Presence of XStream library JAR files in application dependencies
network_indicators: HTTP POST/PUT requests with large or complex XML payloads to /rest/* or similar REST endpoints
Inbound requests containing XML referencing java.lang.ProcessBuilder or other sensitive classes
Outbound network connections initiated by the server following suspicious XML requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic to Struts2 REST endpoints for XML payloads containing references to java.lang.ProcessBuilder or other sensitive classes. Audit application logs for errors or stack traces related to XStream deserialization. Use application firewalls or runtime instrumentation to block or alert on deserialization of untrusted data. Scan application source code and configuration for use of XStream without type whitelisting and for REST plugin enablement.
